youtube.aciklama: The tubing and earmold canal of a behind-the-ear aid also form a resonating tube. These resonances can create clear peaks in the device's frequency response, often near 1000, 3000 and 5000 Hz. An acoustic damper placed in the tubing smooths these peaks; if you see sharp peaks in real-ear measurement, first check the tubing, the earmold canal and the damper.
